title: Chorus: KV fragment mapping and flow-controlled prefetch for multi-GPU pipeline memory
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Large autoregressive workloads with pipeline+tensor parallelism show uneven KV cache memory pressure across GPUs. When continuous batching is enabled, hot-key access patterns and long-context sequences cause frequent cross-GPU KV fetches, triggering spill, stutter in latency p99s, and memory fragmentation.

Goal: Design and implement a coordinated 'fragment mapping' layer (codename Chorus) that: (1) maps KV fragments to GPU-local preferred homes using a workload-aware affinity function; (2) manages small, versioned KV fragments (micro-fragments) to reduce large slab fragmentation; (3) implements flow-controlled cooperative prefetch to stage hot fragments ahead of decode without causing bursty memory pressure; and (4) integrates with scheduler/pipeline to respect tensor-parallel partitioning and minimize cross-device hops.

Scope: Prototype placement + prefetch heuristics in serving runtime, new eviction/spill policy, a lightweight telemetry surface for per-fragment metrics, and an opt-in rollout that can be toggled per-customer or per-model variant.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prototype can map and retrieve KV fragments with <5% added steady-state latency compared to baseline for short contexts (<=1024) and reduces p99 tail during long-context continuous batching workloads by >=20% on internal benchmark suite
Memory fragmentation metric (max GPU free ranges count) reduced by >=25% on multi-GPU long-context traces
No regression in correctness: tokens generated are identical (bitwise) when using Chorus placement vs baseline retrieval for identical inputs
Fallbacks exist: when a fragment is missing locally, cross-GPU fetch latency is measured and bounded; system can disable prefetch for high-load customers without restart
Instrumentation: per-fragment telemetry is emitted (placement, hit/miss, prefetched_by, fetch_latency_ms) and visible in console dashboards
Feature gated and configurable by policy: affinity window size, micro-fragment target size, prefetch concurrency limit, and spill thresholds
tasks: Design affinity function and scoring for fragment->GPU mapping; document assumptions and edge cases
Implement fragment metadata and micro-fragment lifecycle (create, compact, retire) in KV manager
Add cooperative prefetch protocol: requester hints, lease tokens, and backpressure signals
Integrate with runtime scheduler to annotate requests with preferred fragment hints
Implement spill policy adjustments to avoid mass-eviction during aggressive prefetch
Add telemetry hooks and a lightweight metrics schema for fragment diagnostics
Unit + integration tests with simulated tensor+pipeline parallel topologies
Benchmarks: run continuous-batching long-context workload and record cost/latency improvements
Create migration/rollout plan and console toggles for gradual enabling
notes: Chorus intentionally uses micro-fragments (~64KB-256KB) to enable fine-grained placement without high metadata overhead
Affinity will combine static topology hints (tensor split ranges, pipeline stage) with dynamic heat signals (recent hit rate and request locality)
Prefetch must be flow-controlled: use a token bucket per-GPU and a global soft-cap to avoid thrashing when many customers spike
We should prefer local replication of extremely hot fragments if it reduces average cross-GPU hops under memory budget
NUMA and PCIe topology will influence placement decisions; include a topology discovery probe in runtime startup
risks: Inaccurate affinity scoring could cause oscillation: fragments continuously migrate triggering extra network traffic
Aggressive prefetch could increase OOM/eviction storms if burst limits are not respected
Added metadata and bookkeeping could increase CPU overhead on hot serving paths
Cross-device fetch latency varies by instance type and cloud region; hard-coded thresholds may not generalize
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (3 weeks): Design doc + simulation harness. Implement fragment metadata, simple static affinity mapping tied to pipeline stage.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Cooperative prefetch protocol and backpressure; integrate with continuous-batching path; basic metrics emitted.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Optimizations: micro-fragment compaction, hot replication policy, NUMA awareness, and safety toggles.
Phase 4 (1 week): Benchmarks, production canary rollouts, and runbook updates
benchmarks: Internal long-context continuous-batching trace: 8x A100 (tensor-parallel 2, pipeline 4) with mixed prompt lengths 512-16384
Baseline: current runtime-1.23 KV placement and eviction policies
Targets: p50 latency <= baseline, p99 latency reduced by >=20%, GPU memory fragmentation metric reduced by >=25%
test_plan: Unit tests for fragment lifecycle and mapping invariants
Integration: end-to-end retrieval correctness across pipeline/tensor partitions
Load tests: synthetic multi-tenant traces with adversarial hot-key distributions
Chaos: simulate network slowdowns between GPUs to validate backoff and fallback behavior
Performance regression tests against runtime-1.23 on our benchmark suite
rollout_plan: Internal canary on staging fleet with feature gate enabled for debug customers
Small production canary for low-traffic tenants + extended monitoring for 72 hours
Gradual ramp with adaptive prefetch limits and automatic rollback on cost/latency regressions
Expose console controls: enable/disable Chorus per model variant and tuning knobs for power users
